prose:
Alexandra Petri's Atlantic column satirizes the prospect of Jensen Huang using AI to draft an apology after reported personal and national-security controversy. The essay's premise is explicitly conditional: it considers whether this unusually awkward writing task might be a case for delegation, then jokes about the lack of a suitable template.

This is a humor column published on 10 November and newly encountered in the feed, not a new investigation or evidence that a particular email was AI-generated. Imagined apology text and fictional examples must not be treated as authentic messages. The piece supplies no forensic authorship finding, legal conclusion or update to NVIDIA's later reinstatement announcement.
highlights: Petri writes satire rather than an investigative report
Imagined text is not an authentic Huang email
No forensic authorship result or legal finding is supplied
The column predates the later reinstatement announcement
